text:
maya: FYI bringing whirl9b-int4 into larger Dedicated pool. Canary showed a few spikes where GPU memory fragmentation climbed and sparked OOMs during 700-1200 token generations. Seen on two different hosts. Anyone familiar with a short mitigation?

akshay: Do you have the host logs + the serving config? my guess is mixing short/long requests in the same microbatch + lazy slot reclamation.

maya: Logs + config pasted below. Note the allocator warnings and a fallback that reclaimed tiny amounts.
```
[2026-03-28T09:12:03Z] req=ddb42 model=whirl9b-int4 max_new_tokens=900 batch=3 seq_ctx=56 mem_total=12.8GB mem_delta=+4.1GB
[2026-03-28T09:12:03Z] runtime: slab_fragmentation=0.47 kv_slots_free=12
[2026-03-28T09:12:03Z] gpu1: attempt kv_alloc -> OOM at serving/allocator/slab.cc:278
[2026-03-28T09:12:03Z] fallback: prefix_evict reclaimed=64MB; retry -> partially succeeded, request slowed
```
Initial canary config: 
```yaml
model: whirl9b-int4
batching:
  max_batch_size: 6
  batch_timeout_ms: 8
  allow_variable_lengths: true
runtime:
  max_new_tokens_default: 1024
  kv_reclaim: lazy
  slot_compaction: disabled
```

perf-bot: Canary metrics (pool-a): p50=150ms, p95=420ms, p99=2.2s, OOM_count=4/2h, avg_tokens=520

lia: Two quick angles: operational and quality. Operationally, when slab fragmentation > ~0.4 small reclamations don't free contiguous KV ranges and later large allocs fail. Quality-wise, int4 divergence can worsen on long tail generations, so it's worth gating defaults.

akshay: For ops I pushed a lightweight change to prefer like-length requests in microbatches and enabled slot_compaction. Patch I rolled: 
```yaml
batching:
  max_batch_size: 3
  batch_timeout_ms: 5
  length_bucketing: true  # group by max_new_tokens buckets
runtime:
  max_new_tokens_default: 320
  kv_reclaim: eager
  slot_compaction: enabled
  slab_soft_reserve: 512MB
```
Rolled at 09:25.

deploy-bot: Deployment whirl9b-int4 v2026-03-28T09:25 by akshay -> pool-a (canary).

perf-bot: Update @09:50: p99=1.1s, OOM_count=0/30m, fragmentation=0.33, avg_mem_headroom +1.2GB.

lia: Good. A few practical notes:
- Bucketing should use static bins like [0-128,129-320,321-640,641+], prefer strict grouping when forming microbatches.
- Soft reserve gives headroom to avoid mid-batch big allocations; we set slab_soft_reserve=512MB.
- Eager eviction + compaction reduces tail fragmentation but can add small latency hiccups so keep batch_time low.

maya: Ran a quick quality sanity check (400 sample long-form summarization prompts) comparing fp16 vs int4 with the new defaults. Results:
- int4: rougeL delta vs fp16 = -1.3 pts (was -2.7 pts with old defaults)
- latency trade: p95 increased ~5% on average due to compaction/eviction extra work
Conclusion: much better tradeoff.

akshay: Action items:
1) Set whirl9b-int4 model defaults: max_new_tokens_default=320, max_batch_size=3, length_bucketing=true, slot_compaction=enabled, slab_soft_reserve=512MB, kv_reclaim=eager.
2) Add a per-route opt-in for long runs which forces route to fp16 or to a dedicated large-slot pool (with warning).
3) Add a monitor: fragmentation>0.42 or OOMs>0 in 15m -> auto-scale to tertiary pool and notify eng-ml-oncall.
4) Schedule quant sweep: int4 vs int8-hybrid for long-form (lia + maya + perf).

lia: I'll own the sweep. Plan: 24h for full evaluation matrix (rouge/bleu, mem, p99 latency, tokens/cost). Will post results in this thread.

maya: Created tickets ML-9087 (defaults + rollout), ML-9088 (bucketing heuristic RFC), ML-9089 (quant sweep). Also added short-run SOP for on-call: if OOMs observed -> reduce batch to 1-2, set max_new_tokens_default to 128 and enable immediate compaction.

(End)
